summary: How to give an iOS build a launch screen storyboard: either let UE convert a single PNG into a simple storyboard, or build a custom LaunchScreen.storyboard in Xcode and copy it into the project's Build/IOS/Resources/Interface folder.
gotchas: Storyboards are mandatory for App Store and Apple Arcade; static launch screens are rejected
Launch images must be PNG with no alpha channel
Without Storyboard ID/Restoration ID set on the View Controller the app hangs on a black screen
Custom storyboard needs a Mac with Xcode; images must sit in an Assets folder next to the storyboard

summary: Step-by-step setup of an Apple App ID, code signing certificate (automatic via Xcode or manual via Keychain) and provisioning profile, then registering them in UE's iOS project settings to package and deploy iOS/iPadOS/tvOS builds.
keys: iOS Distribution (App Store and Ad Hoc)
gotchas: Requires macOS with Xcode and a paid ($99/yr) Apple Developer account for shipping
Signing certificate in Project Settings must match the one used for the provisioning profile or packaging fails
Xcode-generated development certificates work only on that Mac and not for shipping
Blueprint-only projects can package for iOS from Windows without manual signing

summary: Windows-side checklist for preparing an Android phone for UE deployment: install USB drivers, enable Developer Mode and USB debugging, and verify the connection with adb.
gotchas: Device listed as Unauthorized means the PC's RSA key fingerprint was not accepted
Device may not appear when connected as Media Device (MTP); try Camera (PTP)

summary: How to generate an Android keystore with keytool, place it in the project's Build/Android folder, and fill in Distribution Signing settings so a packaged build can be uploaded to Google Play.
gotchas: Store Version must be incremented on every re-upload or the new APK will be rejected

summary: Run an iOS/iPadOS build as a Designed for iPad or Designed for iPhone app on an Apple Silicon Mac straight from the editor's Quick Launch menu, replacing the Xcode iOS Simulator, with runtime detection and known limitations.
keys: Platforms > Quick Launch Current Level > IOS
gotchas: Requires an Apple Silicon Mac registered as a development device on the signing team
No touchscreen, motion sensors, camera or ARKit; performance not representative of devices
As of macOS 26 spctl --add and other Gatekeeper bypasses no longer work
Personal Team profiles expire every seven days

summary: Platform-agnostic overview of the mobile achievement Blueprint nodes (cache, read progress, write progress, show platform achievement screen) for iOS Game Center and Google Play, using Unreal Match 3 examples.
gotchas: Cache Achievements must succeed before reading cached values
Latent nodes cannot be used inside Functions
Game Center stores progress as an integer (1-100); Google Play uses floats

summary: Configure AdMob banner ads on Android via the Google Play Services project settings and Target.cs modules, then show and hide banners with Blueprint nodes.
gotchas: C++ projects must add OnlineSubsystemGooglePlay, OnlineSubsystem and AndroidAdvertising to ExtraModuleNames in Target.cs

summary: Google Play-specific setup of achievements (Enable Google Play Support, Games App ID, Achievement Map) plus the shared caching, read, write and show-screen achievement Blueprint nodes.
gotchas: For cross-platform iOS/Android, use the iOS Achievement Reference as the Achievement Map Name
Latent nodes cannot be used inside Functions

summary: Reference for the GooglePAD plugin: packaging chunks as install-time, fast-follow or on-demand asset packs in Android App Bundles, excluding chunks from the OBB, and the UGooglePADFunctionLibrary API for requesting, monitoring and removing downloads.
gotchas: Requires Android App Bundle packaging
Max 50 asset packs; one install-time (1 GB) and one fast-follow (512 MB) pack; on-demand packs 512 MB each
Must call ReleaseAssetPackLocation / ReleaseDownloadState to free cached info
Each fast-follow/on-demand pack folder needs a build.gradle file

summary: Set up Google Play leaderboards via the Leaderboard Map in Android project settings and read, write and display them with Blueprint leaderboard nodes.
gotchas: Read Leaderboard Integer is latent; value is 0 before success
iOS and Android leaderboards only accept values higher than currently stored

summary: Short overview of mobile in-game banner ads: links to the AdMob Android setup page and shows the Show Ad Banner and Hide Ad Banner Blueprint nodes.

Explains the mobile store purchase flow (query offers, purchase, server-side receipt validation, grant, finalize) for Google Play and App Store, with Blueprint node references and IOnlineStoreV2/IOnlinePurchase C++ examples, async receipt handling and troubleshooting.
gotchas: Not finalizing transactions can cause refunds on Google Play and performance issues on App Store
Receipts must be validated server-side; subscription status is not available on device
Banking data and legal agreements must be set in store consoles or sandbox testing fails
iOS provisioning profile must include the In-App Purchases entitlement

summary: How to run Lumen on high-end Android Vulkan SM5 devices using the desktop renderer, including the SM5 device profiles and how to match new devices or create Lumen-capable profiles in DeviceProfiles.ini.
gotchas: Experimental; not recommended for shipping
Requires the desktop renderer on Android, which is off by default and costly
Lumen does not work on iOS/tvOS/iPadOS

summary: Enable mesh draw-call auto-instancing on mobile via GPU Scene cvars in DefaultEngine.ini, with a texture-backed option for Mali devices.
gotchas: Beta feature
Triggers mobile shader rebuild
Mali buffers limited to 64 kb, so r.Mobile.UseGPUSceneTexture is needed there
Mainly helps CPU-bound projects

summary: Enable the Mobile FSR plugin (mobile-optimized AMD FSR 1.0 upscaling) and tune its sharpening, denoise and upsampling cvars via console or device profiles.
gotchas: May create artifacts with post-processes that add intentional noise or patterns
r.Mobile.FSR.DisableCompute can help performance on Mali

summary: Platform-agnostic overview of mobile leaderboard Blueprint nodes for Game Center and Google Play: read, write and show the native leaderboard screen.
gotchas: Read Leaderboard Integer is latent and returns 0 until success
Platforms only accept values higher than the stored score

summary: Hub page introducing the three Oodle compression plugins (Oodle Data, Oodle Network, Oodle Texture), all enabled by default, and linking to each one's page.

Use the viewport's Performance and Scalability > Preview Platform menu to emulate Android GLES 3.1, Android Vulkan or iOS Metal rendering and that platform's scalability/device-profile settings in the editor, including generating and loading a device's settings from a Json file.
keys: Preview Android with Json > Preview via Json
gotchas: First switch to a preview level recompiles shaders
Preview may not match the target device exactly; always test on hardware
Android GLES 3.1 and Vulkan levels only appear once enabled as targets in Project Settings

summary: Reference for configrules.txt in Build/Android: version header, auto-defined device variables, set/clear/condition/chipset commands, profile overrides, error/warning dialogs with localized strings, C++ access, and the UPL setup to embed the file in the APK.
gotchas: First line must be exactly '// version:1' and the number must be incremented on each update
Setting the error variable stops processing and blocks the user from continuing
Variables are case-sensitive

summary: Enabling the Vulkan renderer for Android projects: PC driver minimums, checking device support, required Android build settings, packaging/installing the APK, and switching the editor to the Android Vulkan preview.
gotchas: Needs NVIDIA 390.0+ or AMD 17+ drivers to preview on PC
Vulkan preview requires a full shader cache recompile that can take an hour or more
Vulkan device profiles apply on Android 9 or higher

summary: How to enable the PC/console forward and deferred renderer on iOS (Metal Desktop Renderer) and Android Vulkan SM5 devices, with its costs and compatibility.
gotchas: Beta on iOS, experimental on Android Vulkan; not recommended for shipping
Only for SM5-capable mobile devices
Requires editor restart; high resource cost

summary: Explains mobile deferred shading (GBuffer kept in tile memory), how to enable it, when to prefer it over mobile forward, the extra lighting features it enables, its limitations and per-GPU tile-memory behaviour.
gotchas: No MSAA support
With precomputed lighting only DefaultLit and Unlit are available; forward recommended instead
Translucency always uses forward shading
Mali Vulkan limits GBuffer to 128 bits/pixel and 4 input attachments by default

summary: Reference for Unreal Plugin Language (UPL), the XML scripting used by plugins to modify AndroidManifest.xml, iOS plists, gradle files and GameActivity.java at packaging time: variables, conditionals, loops, text insertion, XML editing, file copy/delete and the full list of Android sections and nodes.
gotchas: Sections share state and run in order, so ordering matters; <init> runs once per architecture
Special characters inside <insert> must be escaped
<deleteFiles> can only remove files from BuildDir; writing outside the APK directory is not recommended

summary: Use the Unreal Engine Remote app (iOS/Android) with the RemoteSession plugin to drive a Play-in-Editor or local game session with touch input from a phone on the same network.
gotchas: Mobile device must be on the same network as the workstation
Enabling the plugin requires an editor restart

summary: Hub page for iOS development from Windows, linking to Remote Mac Builds and the Windows Metal Shader Compiler pages.
gotchas: Signed C++ iOS/tvOS builds still require a macOS machine

summary: Explains iOS/tvOS/iPadOS 14+ gamepad/keyboard/mouse support and using the Get Gamepad Button Glyph Blueprint node to show button glyphs that match the user's OS-level remapping.
gotchas: App Store and Apple Arcade may reject apps whose button prompts do not match OS-level remaps

summary: Reference for UnrealBuildTool's BuildConfiguration.xml: where the file is read from on Windows/Mac/Linux and every settable property grouped by section (BuildConfiguration, WindowsPlatform, ModuleConfiguration, UnrealBuildAccelerator, ParallelExecutor, Horde, XGE, ProjectFileGenerator and IDE generators), covering unity builds, PCHs, live coding, parallelism, compiler/toolchain selection and debug info.
gotchas: With bUseUBTMakefiles, adding/removing source files requires regenerating project files or passing -gather
MinCpuArchX64 / bMinCpuArchAPX raise minspec; executables crash on CPUs without AVX/APX
bAllowHybridExecutor is no longer supported
bUseIncrementalLinking is off by default because it can cause PDB-related errors

summary: How to use the Low-Level Memory Tracker (LLM): command-line flags and stat commands to view per-tag memory, CSV output, built-in tag categories, declaring custom tags with LLM_DECLARE_TAG/LLM_DEFINE_TAG/LLM_SCOPE_BYTAG, experimental tag sets, and implementation details.
gotchas: Compiled out of Shipping; in Test it writes CSV but shows no on-screen stats
LLM overhead can be 100MB or more
Tag sets (asset tracking) are experimental and add memory/runtime overhead
LLM_SCOPED_TAG_WITH_STAT style macros are deprecated

summary: Build and run the ASDTool to generate a State Object Database (.sodb) from a cooked Windows D3D12 SM6 build for DirectX Advanced Shader Delivery, so stores precompile PSOs per GPU; also covers compiling and registering PSDBs locally to test.
gotchas: Only Windows D3D12 SM6; ray tracing PSOs not supported
ASDTool must be built from engine source (not in binary builds)
Microsoft Store only for now; Epic Games Store support planned for early 2027
Keep PSO precaching and bundled PSO caches enabled; ASD covers only supported GPUs and recent drivers

summary: Explains automatic PSO precaching (global shaders and components at PostLoad), its cvars, proxy-creation delay strategy, waiting in the loading screen, thread pool and memory tuning, validation stats, Insights/log diagnosis of misses, and C++ extension points for components, vertex factories and mesh pass processors.
gotchas: Loading screen should wait for outstanding precache compiles or components like landscape may pop/hitch
Each PSO compile thread can use up to 2 GB; unbounded thread pools can exhaust memory
Use -clearPSODriverCache for every smoothness test or the driver cache masks hitches
PSO precompile cvars cannot be changed at runtime without engine changes

summary: Hub page introducing the ChunkDownloader plugin, a patching solution for delivering many small files, and pointing to its setup guides.

Overview of BuildGraph, the XML build-automation scripting system for UAT/UBT: tasks, nodes, agents, triggers, aggregates, properties/options, file tagging, and distributed execution flags, with links to the script reference and usage pages.
gotchas: Agents have no effect when building locally
Machine allocation for distributed runs must be managed by an external system

summary: Glossary entry defining BuildGraph as Epic's parameterized build-pipeline scripting language, executed by Horde in jobs created from templates.

Windows walkthrough for turning a source-built engine into a distributable installed build with RunUAT BuildGraph and InstalledEngineBuild.xml, then building ShaderCompileWorker and testing UnrealEditor.exe (written with HMI/Android projects in mind).
gotchas: Needs DotNet 6.0 runtime and, on Windows 10, Debugging Tools for Windows in the SDK
Must pass -set:With[Platform] for every platform you have source for
'Unable to launch ShaderCompileWorker' means SCW was not built separately
Remove -clean if you get an 'Other Compilation Error'

summary: Tutorial for distributing C++ compilation to Horde agents via Unreal Build Accelerator (UBA): BuildConfiguration.xml settings for the Horde server and pool, forcing remote builds, and configuring compute cluster ACLs once authentication is enabled.
gotchas: Requires a Horde Server and agents reachable on ports 7000-7010
UBA supports Windows only (as of 5.5)
Anonymous auth gives everyone full access; switch to Horde or OpenIdConnect
Do not run a Horde Agent on the same machine as the Horde Server

summary: Explains Include-What-You-Use conventions for UE C++ (headers include their own dependencies, .cpp includes its own .h first, no explicit PCH or monolithic headers), how PCHUsage enables it per module, and tips for opting a game module in.
gotchas: IWYU is off by default for games and game plugins, on for engine code
UBT warns if a .cpp does not include its matching header first
Verify compliance by compiling non-unity with PCHs disabled

summary: Reference for making an Installed Build of the engine via BuildGraph's InstalledEngineBuild.xml: command line, all -set: script options (platforms, DDC, configurations, signing, UBA args), InstalledEngineFilters.xml, and registering a custom build identifier so .uproject EngineAssociation matches across a team.
gotchas: iOS/tvOS options need a Mac set up for remote building; console options need their SDKs
Building the stand-alone DDC is one of the slowest steps; skip with -set:WithDDC=false
Installed builds are read-only distributions
